\[
\begin{gathered}
M(\theta) =
\begin{bmatrix} 0.213 & 0.715 & 0.072 \\ 0.213 & 0.715 & 0.072 \\ 0.213 & 0.715 & 0.072 \end{bmatrix}
+ \cos\theta
\begin{bmatrix} 0.787 & -0.715 & -0.072 \\ -0.213 & 0.285 & -0.072 \\ -0.213 & -0.715 & 0.928 \end{bmatrix}
+ \sin\theta
\begin{bmatrix} -0.213 & -0.715 & 0.928 \\ 0.143 & 0.140 & -0.283 \\ -0.787 & 0.715 & 0.072 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad \theta = 90^{\circ}
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(R, G, B\): The encoded channel values from 0 to 255
- \(\theta\): The rotation angle

This is the matrix of the CSS hue-rotate() function in the W3C Filter Effects spec. The first part keeps the gray value, the other two turn the color difference around the gray axis. Grays stay gray. The rotation happens in a luma and chroma plane, not in HSV, so the gray value of each color changes little, but HSV hue does not move by exactly theta. The HSV adjustment filter turns the HSV hue exactly. The matrix acts on the encoded sRGB values from 0 to 255, and the results are clipped to 0 to 255.
